## 0. WHAT THIS IS, AND WHAT IT IS NOT

`GATE4_PREREG.md` already declares **Q5** (line 127, §5.4.1, §11.2.3) and marks it
`⛔ NOT YET ADMISSIBLE — METRIC NOT BUILT, NOT FUZZED (D10)`. The metric was never
implemented: no speaker-embedding field appears anywhere in the Stage 2 rows.

**This document supplies only what the frozen text deliberately left open** — the encoder
set ("named at freeze time by reading the frozen encoder study's own artifact"), the
minimum-duration domain, the dispersion estimand, and the label rules.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Authority** | `GATE4_PREREG.md` **wins on every point it already fixes.** Where this spec appears to differ, the prereg is right and this spec is defective. |
| **Not a reopening** | Gate 4 Stage 1, Stage 2, `GATE3_FREEZE.json`, `GATE4_FREEZE.json`, `GATE4_STAGE2_*` are **read-only here.** No metric, threshold, taxonomy, artifact or verdict of theirs is touched, restated or shadowed. `mcd` remains the only ranking metric in Gate 4; **Q5 ranks nothing.** |
| **Not a pre-registration** | It is a **specification freeze**, in the sense of `GATE4_STAGE2_SPEC.md` §0. See §12 for exactly what the hash does and does not establish. |
| **Two estimands, and only one of them is the frozen Q5** | **Q5-R** (retention) implements frozen Q5. **Q5-D** (within-speaker dispersion of reconstructions) is **NEW in this spec** and is declared as an addition. |
| **Q5-D is NOT Q8** | Frozen **Q8** is *identity drift within a passage* — successive windows of one 14 s decode, `⛔ DEPENDS ON Q5`, declared underpowered. **Q8 stays unbuilt and is out of scope.** Q5-D compares **different recordings**, never windows of one. |

used to interpret a Q5 number is measured in §3 on this corpus.**

## 3. THE QUANTITIES — SEPARATE, AND NEVER COLLAPSED INTO ONE SCORE

All are cosine similarities between L2-normalised embeddings, per encoder.
`i`, `j` index **recordings** (`speaker`, `state`, `index`); `a` indexes arms.

| id | quantity | definition | role |
|---|---|---|---|
| **R** | identity retention | `cos(src_i, recon_i^a)` | frozen Q5 |
| **D_within** | reconstruction dispersion, same state | `cos(recon_i^a, recon_j^a)`, same speaker, **same state**, `i ≠ j` | NEW (Q5-D) |
| **D_cross** | reconstruction dispersion, across states | same, **different states** | NEW (Q5-D) |
| **C_within / C_cross** | **human within-speaker ceiling** | the identical computation on **source** embeddings, same strata | §5.4.1 mandatory calibration |
| **F_src** | **between-speaker floor** | `cos(src_i, src_j)`, **different speakers** | §5.4.1 mandatory calibration |
| **F_rec** | between-speaker floor, reconstructed | `cos(recon_i^a, recon_j^a)`, different speakers | descriptor: impostor inflation |

⛔ **THE CALIBRATION MUST MATCH THE MEASURED DURATION REGIME — added in revision 4.**
`C` and `F` are computed on exactly the signal the measurement compares:

| set | calibration signal |
|---|---|
| **S** | the full source recording (2.54–13.50 s) — what Set S cells measure. **Unchanged from revision 3.** |
| **L** | the **first 14.0 s** of each source recording, cache variant `pre14s` — because Gate 4's Set L cells are 14 s top-rung decodes, not the full 14.7–35.8 s performance |

⚠️ **Why: measured, not argued.** Revision 3 calibrated Set L on full-length audio, which
is trivially more self-similar. The inflation, measured on source audio alone:
`ecapa` **+0.0357** (Neutral) and **+0.0549** (Whisper); `redimnet_M_vb2_ptn` **+0.0203**
and **+0.0307**. The bootstrap intervals are 0.02–0.03 wide, so the bias is as large as the
interval and runs **toward `DRIFTING`**. §8.2 requires `C` to be the identical computation
on the identical stratum; a 22 s ceiling is not the identical stratum for a 14 s
measurement. ⛔ **Set S calibration is untouched, and that it is untouched is verified by
re-hashing its rows against the revision-3 artifact.**

⭐ **Order of computation is fixed: C and F are computed on SOURCE AUDIO ALONE and written
before a single reconstructed file is opened** (§5.4.1: *"the calibration control is
mandatory and is computed on the SOURCE audio alone, before any decoded audio is
scored"*). **An uncalibrated cosine is never reported.** This is **step 2 of the binding
run order in §9.0** — after F1 metric mechanics, which need no corpus statistic, and
before F2, which consumes the ranges calibration produces.

**Pairing rules for every dispersion/floor quantity:**

1. A recording is **never paired with itself.**
2. **Ladder rungs are excluded from all pairwise quantities.** They are repeated measures
   of one performance (§11.2.1); pairing them would measure decoder determinism, not
   identity stability. Rungs enter **only** the duration analysis of **R**.
3. Offline and streamed reconstructions are never paired with each other inside D (§7
   handles that comparison).
4. Pairs cross **texts**, so no pair shares a script line.
   ⛔ **THIS BINDS THE REFERENCE EXACTLY AS IT BINDS THE ESTIMATOR** (§8.2: *identical
   pairing rules*). Revision 5's `q5_calibration.py` applied it to `D` but **not** to
   `C_cross` or `F_src`, so the ceiling admitted the **same script line spoken in two
   states** — in a fully parallel corpus, the most similar cross-state pair that exists —
   and was inflated toward `DRIFTING`. Excess pairs: **3,255 in Set S** (7 speakers × 15
   state-pairs × 31 texts) and **105 in Set L**. **Eight of 108 CROSS labels turned on
   it.** Found by independent audit, repaired in revision 6. **The rule did not change;
   the implementation was wrong.** `Q5_CALIBRATION.json` now records
   `n_pairs_admitted`, which **must equal** the pair count `q5_analyze.py` forms for the
   matching `D` — 97,650 (Set S) and 1,470 (Set L).
5. `F_src` / `F_rec` pair **within the same state** and are reported per state; a floor
   pooled across states is not reported.

⚠️ **Set S and Set L are never pooled into one number.** Different texts, different
duration regimes (2.5–13.5 s vs 14.7–35.8 s). Every table names its set.

## 4. ADMISSIBILITY — AND STAGE 1 SUPPORT AS A COVARIATE ONLY

| state | when | never |
|---|---|---|
| `INADMISSIBLE — BELOW ENCODER MINIMUM` | duration after resampling < 2.00 s | as a number |
| `UNKNOWN` | non-finite samples, or an all-zero / RMS = 0 signal | as 0.0, and never as similarity |
| `NOT MEASURED` | the file does not exist (e.g. a streamed cell an arm never produced) | as an absence of effect |
| `MEASURED` | everything else | — |

**Both sides of every comparison must be admissible, and the worse state wins.** A cosine
needs two signals: if either the source or the reconstruction (or either member of a `D`
pair) is `INADMISSIBLE`, `UNKNOWN` or `NOT MEASURED`, **the cell takes that state and no
number is produced.** Precedence when the two sides differ: `NOT MEASURED` > `UNKNOWN` >
`INADMISSIBLE` > `MEASURED`. The state is recorded per side as well as per cell, so a
source-side refusal can never be read as a property of the arm.

⛔ **STAGE 1 / STAGE 2 SUPPORT STATE IS A DECLARED COVARIATE, NEVER A Q5 EXCLUSION.**
Stage 2 labelled 17,020 of 31,248 offline cells `NOT COMPARABLE — OUTSIDE VALIDATED
SUPPORT` **for `mcd`**. That is a statement about `mcd`'s validated domain, not about the
encoders'. Therefore each Q5 cell carries `support_mcd` (the Stage 2 label) and
`offline_length_state` (Stage 1) as **fields**, every aggregate is printed **twice** —
pooled over admissible cells, and stratified by `support_mcd` — and **no cell is dropped
because of them.** Declared before any Q5 number exists, so it cannot become a filter
chosen for its effect.

⚠️ **Stated with every Q5 table:** a cosine computed on a collapsed or band-limited
reconstruction is a real measurement of what the encoder sees, and it is **not** evidence
that the arm is a functioning decoder. The support stratification exists so a reader can
see which is which.

## 5. UNIT, AGGREGATION, UNCERTAINTY — INHERITED VERBATIM FROM §11.2

| | |
|---|---|
| experimental unit | **the RECORDING** (§11.2.1). Cells are never independent observations. |
| interval | **cluster bootstrap over recordings, with replacement, `n_resamples = 4000`, `seed = 20260911`, percentile interval at 95 %** (§11.2.2) |
| point estimate | the **median** (§13, descriptive as primary) |
| aggregation path | `cell → recording → (speaker × state) → arm` — **within (speaker × state) first, then across**, so a speaker with more admissible recordings cannot dominate (§11.2.3) |
| ladder | rungs travel with their recording: a recording contributes **all** its cells or none (§11.2.2) |
| paired estimands | resample the recording **once**, take both arms'/conditions' values from that draw (§11.2.2) |
| hypothesis tests | **none. No p-values, no significance claims** (§11.2.4). Intervals and effect sizes only. |

### 5.1 ⛔ THE AGGREGATION GROUP OF A PAIR — revision 5, and it must be order-invariant

§11.2.3 aggregates `within (speaker × state) first, then across`. A **pair** in a CROSS
stratum spans two states, so that rule does not name its group, and revision 4's
implementation silently used **the lower-indexed member's** group.

⚠️ **MEASURED, on the existing data, 6 permutations per stratum, identical bootstrap
draws so that the grouping is the only thing varying:** permuting row order moved the
CROSS median by up to **0.089** and the interval bounds by up to **0.079**
(`mimi_q8` · `ecapa` · Set S). Interval widths are 0.02–0.03, so an arbitrary row order
could flip a CROSS label. **That is a defect, not a convention.**

> **The group of a pair is the components its two members' groups SHARE.**
> Within a state, both members carry `(speaker, state)` → the group is
> `(speaker, state)`. Across states they share only the speaker → the group is
> `(speaker,)`. Both pairs of a symmetric relation give the same answer, so the estimator
> **cannot depend on row order.**

**Verified, not asserted:** re-running the same strata under 6 permutations gives a spread
of **0.00e+00** on median, `lo` and `hi` (float noise ≤ 2.2e-16). ⛔ **Within-state
quantities are unchanged by construction** — the shared components of two identical group
tuples are that tuple — and that invariance is re-verified by re-hashing the within-state
calibration rows against the previous artifact.

**Dispersion bootstrap, declared because §11.2 does not cover pairwise quantities:**
resample **recordings** (not pairs); recompute the pairwise set using only pairs between
**distinct sampled recordings**; a draw yielding fewer than 3 distinct recordings in a
stratum contributes no value. **A stratum with fewer than 3 distinct admissible recordings
gets no interval at all and is labelled `NOT ESTABLISHED`** — it never gets a point
estimate dressed as a result.

**Reporting grid, declared as a grid and not a test family:** 18 arms × 3 encoders ×
{S, L} × states. No multiplicity correction is applied because no test is performed.

## 6. STRATIFICATION — WHAT IS ALWAYS BROKEN OUT

Speaker (7) · state (**Neutral, Angry, Happy, Scared, Shouting, Whisper** in Set S;
**Neutral, Whisper** in Set L) · set (**S / L / ladder**) · arm (18) · encoder (3) ·
`support_mcd`. Duration enters only through the ladder, reported as repeated measures on
its 4 texts × 7 speakers × 2 states, with the **text-level n printed on every rung
aggregate** (§Q4 M11).

⛔ **CROSS-ARM DURATION COMPARISON USES 5 s, 10 s AND 14 s ONLY — revision 4, measured.**
The 1 s rung is inadmissible everywhere. **The 2 s rung is admissible in 11 arms and
inadmissible in 7**, because realised reconstruction lengths at that nominal rung span
**1.9199–2.0434 s** and the frozen 2.00 s minimum cuts through them. The arms surviving at
2 s are therefore **selected by their own output-length behaviour**, which is selection on
an arm property, and no cross-arm statement may rest on it. ⛔ **The 2.00 s threshold is
NOT relaxed to rescue that rung** — the rung is reported per arm and excluded from
cross-arm comparison, and the 1 s rung stays inadmissible.

## 7. OFFLINE vs STREAMED — A DETECTOR, NOT A RANKING

Answers one question: *does streaming cost identity beyond what this arm's own
full-context decode already costs?*

- `S1 = cos(recon_offline_i^a, recon_streamed_i^a)` — self-consistency across conditions.
- `S2 = R_streamed_i^a − R_offline_i^a` — paired retention delta, same recording.

**16 arms only.** A cell with no streamed output is `NOT MEASURED`. ⛔ **Never merged with
R, never phrased as one arm being better than another, and never used in a label of §8.**

## 8. LABELS — COMPLETELY MECHANICAL. NO QUALITATIVE WORDING SURVIVES HERE.

⚠️ **Revision 2 rewrote this section.** Revision 1's rules used the phrases *"not below
the human band"*, *"at least as tight"* and *"measurably looser"* in prose beside the
inequalities. Prose beside an inequality is a second rule that can be read differently
once results are visible. **Everything below is an inequality on named estimands.**

### 8.1 The labelling unit

A label is assigned per **(arm `a`, encoder `e`, set ∈ {S, L}, stratum)**, where
`stratum` is either **one state** (within-state) or **`CROSS`** (different states, same
speaker). Set S yields 6 within-state strata + `CROSS`; Set L yields 2 + `CROSS`.
**Ladder cells never carry a label** (§3, rule 2). There is no arm-level label and no
encoder-pooled label.

⛔ **WHICH CELL IS THE LABEL CELL — corrected in revision 4, and the correction is why
revision 4 exists.** Selection is **by set**, never by the presence of a rung:

| set | label cell | n per arm |
|---|---|---|
| **S** | the Set S cell (no rung) | 1,302 |
| **L** | **the 14 s top-rung cell, one per recording** | 210 |
| **L_ladder** | ⛔ **none.** Sub-rungs are repeated measures (§3 rule 2) and feed **only** the duration analysis | 224 |

⚠️ **Revision 3's analysis selected label cells with `rung_s is None`.** Every Set L cell
carries `rung_s = 14.0`, because Gate 4 measures Set L on its declared 14 s top rung, so
that filter **silently dropped all 210 Set L recordings per arm** and would have returned
`NOT ESTABLISHED — fewer than 3 distinct admissible recordings` for every Set L stratum —
a true-looking refusal string hiding half the design. **No label had been computed when
this was found.**

⚠️ **The two stratum kinds carry DIFFERENT label vocabularies, added in revision 2 to close
a category error.** `C_cross` measures how far apart two recordings **in different states**
sit, which is a far lower ceiling than within-state; reading a retention value against it
would flatter every arm.

| stratum kind | reference | labels available |
|---|---|---|
| **within-state** (one state) | `C̃_within` of **that same state** | the full four of §8.4 |
| **`CROSS`** | `C̃_cross` | **dispersion only: `CROSS-STATE CONSISTENT` (`D.lo ≥ C.lo`) · `CROSS-STATE DRIFTING` (`D.hi < C.lo`) · `NOT ESTABLISHED`** |

⛔ **`R` is ALWAYS read against the within-state `C̃` of the recording's own state, and
never against `C̃_cross`.** The `CROSS` stratum therefore carries **no** `PRESERVED` and
**no** `STABLE OFFSET` verdict — those require `R`, and `R` has no cross-state reference.

### 8.2 The four estimands, named exactly

All are computed by the §5 procedure — cluster bootstrap over recordings, 4 000
resamples, seed 20260911, 95 % percentile interval, median point estimate, aggregated
within (speaker × state) then across. **Cosine: higher = more similar.**

| symbol | estimand | over |
|---|---|---|
| `R̃`, `[R.lo, R.hi]` | median of `R` = `cos(src_i, recon_i^a)` | admissible recordings in (a, e, set, stratum). For `CROSS`, all states pooled by the §5 path. |
| `D̃`, `[D.lo, D.hi]` | median of `cos(recon_i^a, recon_j^a)`, same speaker, `i ≠ j`, pairs obeying §3's five pairing rules | admissible pairs in (a, e, set, stratum) |
| `C̃`, `[C.lo, C.hi]` | median of `cos(src_i, src_j)`, same speaker, `i ≠ j`, **identical pairing rules, identical strata, source audio only** | the matching (e, set, stratum) |
| `F_hi` | the **95th percentile** of `cos(src_i, src_j)` across **different** speakers, computed once at calibration (§9 step 2) and frozen in `Q5_CALIBRATION.json` | the matching (e, set, state); for `CROSS`, the max of `F_hi` over that set's states |

**The matching rule for `C̃` is strict and total:** same encoder, same set, same stratum.
A Set S Whisper label may only be read against Set S Whisper's `C̃`. **No substitution, no
pooled ceiling, no ceiling borrowed from another set, state or encoder, and no value from
the published encoder study.**

⚠️ **`C̃` is the reference because §5.4.1 requires it**, and it answers the only question
that has a scale: did the route move the voice **more than this speaker's own two
recordings differ from each other**? The upper reference for `R` is 1.0 (identical audio)
and it is never used as the comparison band.

### 8.3 The definitions, as inequalities

| phrase used anywhere in Q5 output | means exactly |
|---|---|
| retention is **inside** the human band | `R.lo ≥ C.lo` |
| retention is **below** the human band | `R.hi < C.lo` |
| the cluster is **as tight as** the human's | `D.lo ≥ C.lo` |
| the cluster is **looser** than the human's | `D.hi < C.lo` |
| `APPROACHES IMPOSTOR RANGE` | `D.lo ≤ F_hi` |

⛔ **Those five lines are the only meanings these phrases may carry in any Q5 table,
report sentence, commit message or summary.**

### 8.4 The label rules

Evaluated in this order. The first rule whose condition holds assigns the label.

| # | label | condition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **INCONSISTENT / DRIFTING** | `D.hi < C.lo` — assigned **whatever `R` says**. Carries the marker `APPROACHES IMPOSTOR RANGE` iff `D.lo ≤ F_hi`. |
| 2 | **PRESERVED + CONSISTENT** | `D.lo ≥ C.lo` **and** `R.lo ≥ C.lo` |
| 3 | **STABLE OFFSET** | `D.lo ≥ C.lo` **and** `R.hi < C.lo` |
| 4 | **NOT ESTABLISHED** | anything else |

**The four are mutually exclusive by construction, not by convention.** `D.lo ≤ D.hi`, so
rules 1 and {2,3} cannot both hold. `R.lo ≤ R.hi`, so `R.lo ≥ C.lo` and `R.hi < C.lo`
cannot both hold, which separates 2 from 3. Order is stated anyway so the implementation
has no freedom.

⭐ **A positive label REQUIRES a resolved dispersion.** If `C.lo ≤ D.hi` and
`D.lo < C.lo` — the intervals overlap — the result is `NOT ESTABLISHED` **even when `R` is
perfectly clear**. Retention alone can never earn `PRESERVED` or `STABLE OFFSET`, because
the thing being claimed is stability.

### 8.5 `NOT ESTABLISHED` fires, mechanically, when

any of: the §8.4 conditions all fail · fewer than **3 distinct admissible recordings** in
the stratum (R) or fewer than **3 distinct admissible recordings contributing pairs** (D)
· `C̃` unavailable or itself refused for that stratum · fewer than **2 speakers** with
admissible recordings, so `F_hi` cannot be computed · every cell in the stratum returned
`INADMISSIBLE`, `UNKNOWN` or `NOT MEASURED` · the encoder was **removed** or **demoted to
DETECTOR** by §9 · the encoder failed §9 step 2's separability gate in that stratum.

Each refusal is written to `Q5_RESULTS.json` **with its reason string**, one of the causes
above and no other. ⛔ **`NOT ESTABLISHED` is never narrowed by widening an interval,
lowering a count, adding a constant, pooling strata, or relabelling after the fact.** It
is expected to be common, especially in Set L, where a stratum holds 105 recordings across
7 speakers but only 15 texts, and in every FocalCodec arm.

### 8.6 Encoders are never merged

Each encoder's labels stand alone. The report prints, per (arm, set, stratum), the
agreement count **3/3, 2/3, 1/3** and **names the dissenting encoder**. ⛔ **No majority
vote, no pooled label, no averaged cosine, no sentence of the form "speaker identity is
preserved" without an encoder name attached.**

## 9. INSTRUMENT VALIDATION AND THE RUN ORDER (R19 / D10)

⚠️ **Revision 2 fixed a circularity in revision 1.** Revision 1 scheduled the whole fuzz
gate before calibration, while one of its probes required a signal to *"land in the
measured `F_src` band"* — a band that does not exist until calibration has run. It also
demoted a metric whose 1-sample response was *"comparable to genuine codec-scale change"*,
which is **a reconstructed-output quantity**: the rule could not be evaluated without the
results it was supposed to gate. **Both are resolved by splitting validation into two
stages either side of calibration, and by pricing the shift response against a
SOURCE-measured range.**

**Declare the domain, never enumerate the failures.** The report says *"survived N
probes"*, never *"closed"*.

### 9.0 ⭐ THE RUN ORDER. BINDING. NO STAGE MAY BE REORDERED.

| # | stage | material | writes | may it see reconstructions? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **F1 — metric mechanics** (§9.1). Needs no corpus statistic. | the **126 calibration recordings** of `GATE4_CORPUS.json → cells.calibration`, declared disjoint from Set S and Set L | `Q5_FUZZ.json → F1` | **NO** |
| **2** | **Source calibration** (§3, §5.4.1). Produces `C̃`, `F_src`, `F_hi`, and the separability gate of §9.2. | **source only**, Set S + Set L | `Q5_CALIBRATION.json` | **NO** |
| **3** | **F2 — calibrated tier gates** (§9.3). Consumes step 2's ranges. | step 1's recorded responses + step 2's ranges | `Q5_FUZZ.json → F2` | **NO** |
| **4** | **Offline cells** — `R`, and the pairs feeding `D`, 18 arms | offline WAVs | `Q5_CELLS.jsonl`, `Q5_EMBEDDINGS.npz` | yes |
| **5** | **Streamed detector** (§7), 16 arms | streamed WAVs | `Q5_CELLS.jsonl` (condition = streamed) | yes |
| **6** | **Analysis, intervals, labels** (§5, §8) | steps 2–5 | `Q5_RESULTS.json` | yes |

⛔ **Steps 1–3 complete, and every encoder's verdict is written, before a single
reconstructed file is opened.** `q5_run.py` **refuses to start** unless
`Q5_FUZZ.json` contains both an `F1` and an `F2` section and `Q5_CALIBRATION.json` exists,
and it refuses per encoder if that encoder was `REMOVED`. This is checked, not documented.

⛔ **No stage looks at a reconstructed output to decide how to measure.** Every constant in
§9.3 is fixed by this document and every range it uses is measured on **source audio**.

### 9.1 F1 — metric mechanics. Source probe material, no corpus statistic

Probe set: the **126 calibration recordings** (7 speakers × 6 states × 3 texts, 1.82–4.96 s,
declared disjoint from both study sets). ⚠️ Recordings shorter than 2.00 s are used **only**
for the truncation and admissibility probes, never for a similarity probe.

| probe | required response | failure means |
|---|---|---|
| the identical file, twice through the encoder | `cos = 1.0` to `atol 1e-6`, and `max_abs_err == 0.0` **exactly** between the two embeddings | ⛔ **the encoder is REMOVED from the panel**, not adjusted (§6) — subject to the one pre-declared device retry below |
| the same, **after a fresh process load** | `max_abs_err == 0.0` exactly against the in-process value | ⛔ **REMOVED.** Stage 2 M3 found a real cold-start effect on `fish_modified_dac`, which is why this probe exists |

⭐ **The device rule, declared in advance so it is not an escape hatch invented on
failure.** The probes run on the declared default device (CUDA if present, else CPU). If an
encoder fails an exact-zero determinism probe there, **exactly one** retry is permitted, on
**CPU with `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` and `torch.set_num_threads(1)`**. The
device that passes becomes **that encoder's declared device for every subsequent step**, is
recorded in `Q5_FUZZ.json`, and may not change again. **If neither device passes, the
encoder is REMOVED.** ⛔ No third device, no relaxed tolerance, no averaging over runs.
| NaN / inf injected | `UNKNOWN` | ⛔ **REMOVED** |
| all-zero signal, and RMS = 0 | `UNKNOWN`, never a number, never ranked above a damaged signal | ⛔ **REMOVED** |
| truncated to 1.99 s | `INADMISSIBLE — BELOW ENCODER MINIMUM` | ⛔ **REMOVED** |
| shifted by **1** sample | response **recorded** as `shift1[e]` = median over probes of `1 − cos(x, shift(x,1))` | gate deferred to §9.3 |
| shifted by 4 / 16 / 256 samples | recorded as a sensitivity curve | descriptive |
| scaled ×0.5 and ×2.0 | response recorded as `scale[e]` = median of `1 − cos(x, k·x)` | gate deferred to §9.3 |
| band-limited to 8 kHz and 4 kHz | recorded per encoder — the narrowband signature several arms produce | descriptive |

### 9.2 The separability gate — source only, and it replaces the deleted floor probe

Revision 1's *"a different speaker must land in the measured floor"* probe is **deleted as
a probe and reinstated as a gate**, because `cos(src_i, src_j)` across speakers **is**
`F_src` by construction: the probe and the quantity are the same computation, so the probe
could never fail independently.

**What is actually gated, per encoder and per (set, state), on source audio alone:**

> **`C̃_within.lo > F_hi`** — the encoder's within-speaker interval must sit strictly above
> the 95th percentile of its between-speaker distribution **on this corpus**.

If it does not, that encoder is **`NOT COMPETENT ON THIS MATERIAL`** for that stratum, it
**assigns no label there** (§8.5), and the fact is reported in full. ⚠️ This is a statement
about that checkpoint on this corpus, **never** about the encoder's general quality — the
`detectorproof` refusal, applied to an encoder panel.

### 9.3 F2 — the calibrated tier gates. Constants fixed here, ranges measured on source

Define, per encoder `e`, from step 2 and **nothing else**:

> **`G(e) = median over Set S states of ( C̃_within(e, state) − F_hi(e, state) )`**

`G(e)` is the encoder's **usable range on this corpus**: the distance between "the same
person again" and "a different person", in cosine, measured on source audio only.

| gate | rule | consequence |
|---|---|---|
| **the tier test** | `shift1[e] > 0.10 × G(e)` | `spk_cos` is **DEMOTED TO DETECTOR** for encoder `e`: it is reported, and it **assigns no label in §8** |
| **scale invariance** | `scale[e] > 0.10 × G(e)` | **DEMOTED TO DETECTOR** for `e`. L2-normalisation predicts ≈ 0; this verifies it |

**The constant 0.10 is declared here, before any reconstruction is opened, and it is a
fraction of a source-measured range — never of a codec result.** Rationale, fixed in
advance: an instrument that moves more than a tenth of its usable range under a
one-sample shift cannot support a distinction between a shifted identity and a wandering
one, which is the only thing Q5 exists to separate. ⛔ **It may not be changed after step 4
begins; a change requires `freeze_q5.py --revise` and is visible in `superseded`.**

## 10. RETAINED ARTIFACTS — WHAT MAKES THE WAVs DELETABLE

**Cache key, and it is the whole point:**
`sha256(wav bytes) · encoder_id · checkpoint_sha256 · **device** · resampler_params ·
pooling_id · spec_revision`. Every embedding therefore proves which bytes produced it,
**and on which hardware**, after those bytes are gone.

⭐ **`device` added in revision 3, provenance only.** Revision 2's key omitted it. Nothing
could exploit that — §9.1 pins one device per encoder and every runner reads that same
mapping — but an embedding that cannot say which hardware produced it is not fully
provenanced, and §9.1's own device rule only means something if the device travels with
the number. Every persisted row and every panel record also carries `device`. ⛔ **The
revision changes no panel member, no device assignment, no threshold, no label rule, no
bootstrap, no admissibility state and no interpretation** — and the ceilings and floors it
produces must reproduce the revision-2 values exactly. `gate4_retro_sha.py` already verified 216/216 on file and sample identity
for the 18 arms; Q5 keys to the same hashes.

| artifact | holds |
|---|---|
| `Q5_EMBEDDINGS.npz` | one embedding per (file × encoder), keyed as above |
| `Q5_CELLS.jsonl` | per (recording × arm × condition × encoder): R, admissibility state, `support_mcd`, `offline_length_state`, durations, **source sha256 and reconstruction sha256** |
| `Q5_CALIBRATION.json` | C_within, C_cross, F_src, F_hi — the ceiling and floor, source-first — plus `G(e)`, every §9.2 separability verdict, and `n_pairs_admitted`. ⛔ **`F_rec` is NOT COMPUTED and no label or gate uses it** — revision 5's table claimed it was here and that was false; it is declared absent rather than invented to match the prose |
| `Q5_RESULTS.json` | every aggregate, interval, label, encoder-agreement count, and every refusal with its reason |
| `Q5_FUZZ.json` | §9's report in **two sections**: `F1` (mechanics, written at step 1) and `F2` (the calibrated tier gates, written at step 3). Each encoder's verdict — `OK`, `DEMOTED TO DETECTOR`, `REMOVED` — is recorded with the number that caused it |
| `Q5_SPEC.md` + `Q5_SPEC_FREEZE.json` | this document and its hash |

### 10.1 ⛔ A SPEC REVISION MUST NOT CAUSE A RE-MEASUREMENT — revision 4

The revision id is part of the cache key, so a naive re-run under a new revision would
re-embed every cell. **It must not.** The revision-3 offline measurement — **18 arms,
93,744 rows, 89,544 MEASURED, 4,200 INADMISSIBLE, 95,214 embeddings, exit 0, drift 0,
8 h 46 m** — is **frozen evidence that revision 4 CONSUMES, not evidence revision 4
regenerates.** Three things make that hold rather than hope it:

1. Each row stores its own `src_emb_key` / `rec_emb_key`; the analysis looks up those
   **stored** strings, so a revision bump cannot orphan an embedding.
2. `q5_run.py` **refuses** to measure a cell already recorded under a different spec
   revision unless `--allow-respec` is passed, and prints what it would have recomputed.
3. Revision 4 changes **no** measured value: not `R`, not an embedding, not an
   admissibility state, not a device, not a threshold, not an inequality, not the
   bootstrap. It changes which cells the analysis selects, the duration regime of the Set L
   calibration, and one covariate lookup.

⚠️ **New source embeddings ARE computed for the Set L `pre14s` calibration.** ⛔ Revision
4's note said that signal "was never embedded before"; **that was wrong** — 210 `pre14s`
source embeddings per encoder already existed from revision 3, as the source side of the
14 s cells. What is new is their use as the Set L **calibration reference**. Either way
this is source audio, never a re-measurement of a reconstruction.

### 10.2 The covariate repair, and why it does not touch the evidence

`offline_length_state` reads `NOT RECORDED` for `fish_modified_dac` (5,208 rows) because
that arm's Stage 1 rows live in `results\gate4_stage1_fish.jsonl`, which revision 3's
lookup did not read. **The rows are not rewritten.** The analysis reads the Stage 1 files
directly — **all three** of them (`decbench`, `decbench_melflow`, `fish`; revision 4's
text said "both", which was wrong) — and records the list it read in
`Q5_RESULTS.json → length_state_lookup.files_read`. Evidence produced by a frozen run
is never edited in place to make it look better.

⛔ **A WAV may be deleted only when these exist, `freeze_q5.py --verify` reports drift 0,
and Stage 2's own deletion preconditions in `STORAGE_LEDGER.md` §3 are met.** Deletion is
recorded in the ledger with its date. **Nothing is deleted by this layer.**

## 11. REFUSALS — DECLARED NOW SO THEY CANNOT BE NEGOTIATED LATER

No encoder added or swapped after results exist · no threshold, constant or exclusion
introduced after results exist · no encoder scores merged or averaged · no ranking of arms
from Q5 (`mcd` remains Gate 4's only ranking metric) · no perceptual or MOS claim · no
cloning claim (§5.5) · no re-running, re-scoring or re-analysing the frozen encoder study
· no modification of any Gate 4 frozen artifact · no audio generated, copied, moved or
deleted · no download of any checkpoint · no absolute Q5 value compared against published
VoxCeleb figures.

## 12. ⛔ WHAT THE HASH DOES AND DOES NOT ESTABLISH

**Establishes:** this specification is fixed, hashed and auditable, it did not move
between `--freeze-spec` and `--freeze`, and **no Q5 result artifact existed on disk at
spec-freeze time** — `freeze_q5.py --freeze-spec` refuses if one does, and records the
check.

**Does NOT establish:** that the spec preceded every line of implementation. Both
timestamps are local `time.gmtime()` with no external anchor, this tree is **not a git
repository**, and `Q5_SPEC_FREEZE.json` is a plain rewritable file. The same withdrawal
that audit 3 forced on `GATE4_STAGE2_FREEZE.json` (M5) applies here in advance: ⛔ **no
ordering proof is claimed.**

**It is not blind.** The author has read Stage 2's results and `EXP_SPK`'s ECAPA numbers.
What freezing buys is that the decisions above are **declared, fixed and auditable before
any Q5 number exists** — not that they are uninfluenced. R19: **the author is not the
certifier.** This spec expects an independent audit before any Q5 result is called final.
